newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS- Sainsbury shares boosted on sales.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS- Sainsbury shares boosted on sales.

text.p: British supermarket group J. Sainsbury Plc lifted its share price on Wednesday with better than expected sales figures as it targeted volume growth of one to two percent this year.

"We intend to sustain positive like-for-like volume growth of between one and two percent for the current year and to increase market share at a faster rate," chairman David Sainsbury told the annual meeting.
He said same store sales since the start of the current financial year were up 4.2 percent, maintaining the growth seen at final results two months ago.
Total sales were up 8.3 percent while inflation has declined to less than one percent growth, he added, with market share at the end of March at 12.6 percent, up from 12.5 percent a year earlier.

But he said sales inflation could fall further until late summer while gross margins remained stable, although analysts said that strong overall official inflation figures for June could prove positive for the sector.

Shares jumped on Sainsbury's comments, rising 11.5p to 399.5 pence by 1440 GMT, lifting other stocks in the sector as well. Tesco, which has overtaken Sainsburys as market leader, gained 14.5 pence to 423p.
"Basically it is good news, ahead of market expectations and ours, at 3-3/4 percent," said one dealer in the stock.

Sainsbury told the annual meeting that the group planned to keep net margins stable with last year's levels or above, before costs associated with ensuring computer systems can cope with the date change in 2000.
Sainsburys is trying to turn around its fortunes after two successive years of falling profits and being overtaken by arch-rival Tesco.
Sainsbury said the group's key strategies were to improve product quality and choice, build customer loyalty, provide consistent product availability and deliver high standards of service.

Chief executive Dino Adriano had indicated in May at annual results that market share leadership was not the sole aim of the group, as year pretax profits fell 15 percent to 651 million pounds ($1.1 billion).
Adriano said market share was not a goal on its own, adding that he considered "rebuilding our superiority in quality and choice is the key to maintaining our sales and market share momentum."
Sainsbury told the annual meeting that "the recovery of Sainsbury's supermarkets will not be an overnight phenomenon but a process of consistent and far-reaching improvement is well underway."
Sainsbury told the annual meeting that like-for-like sales at its Homebase home improvement chain grew nine percent in the first 16 weeks of the current year although sales of kitchens remained poor.
Sales at the group's Savacentre hypermarkets and its U.S. unit Shaw's remained stable, Sainsbury added.
At its Sainsbury's Bank joint venture with Bank of Scotland, there are now 300,000 accounts with deposits of over half a billion pounds, Sainsbury said.

Sainsburys was the first of the main supermarkets to launch a bank after following Tesco's lead into financial services once it had made an embarrassing U-turn and launched its Reward loyalty card to compete with Tesco's boosted sales from its ClubCard version.
Sainsbury's Bank has already launched personal loans and will be introducing mortgages "in the weeks to come," Sainsbury added.
Reward now has over nine million holders, Sainsbury said, with loyalty card sales accounting for over 80 percent of total. ($ = 0.592 British Pounds)
